chalisa.do1: Bowing to the lotus feet of Śrī Guru and setting right my faulty thoughts, I describe the spotless fame of Rāṇī Satī as far as my understanding allows.
chalisa.do2: The world has been wandering astray in desire, anger, pride and greed. When one takes refuge in the compassionate Mother, happiness and wealth flow in.
chalisa.cau1: Salutations, salutations to Śrī Satī Bhavānī, famed throughout the world and honoured in every heart. ॥1॥
chalisa.cau2: Salutations, salutations to her who removes troubles and fulfils every desire of the heart. ॥2॥
chalisa.cau3: Salutations, salutations, victory, victory to you, Jagadambā, Mother of the world; your devotees' tasks suffer no delay. ॥3॥
chalisa.cau4: Salutations, salutations, victory, victory to you who carry the world across, who set right the tasks of your servants. ॥4॥
chalisa.cau5: Your form is divine, and a coloured veil graces your head; glittering earrings charm the mind. ॥5॥
chalisa.cau6: Vermilion is in the parting of your hair, with fine kohl and a forehead ornament; your nose-ring of elephant pearls is lovely and fine. ॥6॥
chalisa.cau7: The vaijayantī garland graces your neck; all sixteen adornments are arrayed on your body. ॥7॥
chalisa.cau8: Blessed is the fortune of Gurasāmala: the Satī was born to him at Ḍokavā near Maham. ॥8॥
chalisa.cau9: She found a worthy husband in Tanadhanadāsa; joy and blessings kept growing. ॥9॥
chalisa.cau10: Becoming the bride of Jālīrāma's son, she made holy the line of both families. ॥10॥
chalisa.cau11: Her lord and husband fell fighting in battle; taking the form of the Satī, she slew the enemies. ॥11॥
chalisa.cau12: Taking her husband with her, she attained the blessed state; the gods, glad at heart, showered flowers. ॥12॥
chalisa.cau13: Blessed, blessed is that Rāṇājī, who saw the Satī and was fulfilled. ॥13॥
chalisa.cau14: In the Vikrama year thirteen hundred and fifty-two, on the ninth of the dark fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa, a Tuesday, ॥14॥
chalisa.cau15: the Mother appeared in the town of Jhunjhunu, famed throughout the world and giver of great blessing. ॥15॥
chalisa.cau16: Pilgrims come from distant lands and offer incense, lamps and food. ॥16॥
chalisa.cau17: They leap up and down with joy, and worship with body, mind and wealth, and with coconuts. ॥17॥
chalisa.cau18: They make the vowed pilgrimage and the first tonsure and keep vigil through the night; all the Bansal clan worship her. ॥18॥
chalisa.cau19: Brahmins perform worship, recitation and reading, and chant the sound of the Vedas. ॥19॥
chalisa.cau20: With delicacies of many different kinds, brahmins are invited and fed. ॥20॥
chalisa.cau21: With faith and devotion they rejoice; her servants obtain the fruit their hearts desire. ॥21॥
chalisa.cau22: Men and women raise cries of victory and give themselves to Śrī Rāṇī Satī. ॥22॥
chalisa.cau23: At the gate of the rampart the nobat sounds every day; she is adorned, and the adornment is arrayed most beautifully. ॥23॥
chalisa.cau24: The jewelled throne gleams finely; every moment, every instant, the Satī is meditated upon. ॥24॥
chalisa.cau25: On the new-moon day of the dark fortnight of Bhādrapada her divine play is celebrated, and a colourful, festive fair gathers. ॥25॥
chalisa.cau26: There is a dense crowd of devotees and good people; there is no room to move for those who come to see her. ॥26॥
chalisa.cau27: Your light stands unshaken in the world; you are a mass of splendour, a brightness in the world. ॥27॥
chalisa.cau28: Your light has merged with the Primal Śakti; in land after land its glory is great. ॥28॥
chalisa.cau29: People worship you in many ways; night and day they hold you in meditation. ॥29॥
chalisa.cau30: You remove hardship and destroy sorrow; you are compassionate, and dwell at Jhunjhunu. ॥30॥
chalisa.cau31: The first Satī was named Nārāyaṇī; twelve more came to be at this very shrine. ॥31॥
chalisa.cau32: Her fame has spread through the three worlds; the name of Śrī Rāṇī Satī is proclaimed everywhere. ॥32॥
chalisa.cau33: Morning and evening the āratī is waved; the nobat and the bells ring out. ॥33॥
chalisa.cau34: Instruments play in all thirty-six rāgas; all thirteen pavilions are most beautifully adorned. ॥34॥
chalisa.cau35: Save me, save me; I am in your refuge. Fulfil the hope in your servant's heart. ॥35॥
chalisa.cau36: My one trust is in you; come and set my affairs right. ॥36॥
chalisa.cau37: I do not know worship, japa, austerity or observance; every day I tell of your pure glory. ॥37॥
chalisa.cau38: You take away your devotees' calamities and grant sons, grandsons, boons and wealth. ॥38॥
chalisa.cau39: For whoever reads this Chālīsā a hundred times, what he has resolved in his mind is accomplished. ॥39॥
chalisa.cau40: Gopīrāma has taken your refuge; forgive all our failings. ॥40॥
chalisa.do3: Remover of sorrow, adversity and calamity, support of the life of the world, set right what has gone wrong, overlooking all offences.
